title: letter-edit
desc: The letter-edit guard on HANDOFF.md. Rule order since 2026-09-02: not-the-letter, first-letter-of-session, unrecorded work in tree, else wishes-under-half refuses. Carries the wish/row deadlock that forced the change and how it was proved closed.
steps: TODO: verify wish-score-ratchet and the PreToolUse letter-edit gate share ONE wish-count implementation so they never disagree again. TRIGGER: an edit to HANDOFF.md is refused with 'POOR COOPERATION with your senior: N of M wishes granted. Go and do the work properly, now.' WHEN: mid-descent, writing or amending the letter. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto to read the refusal as three separate claims, close the ONE wish it names, and only then return to the letter. THE THRESHOLD IS HALF -- Test-WkLetterEditAllowed.ps1 line 99 reads 'At or above half: through, and silent', so 0 of 14 means seven wishes must be granted before the letter opens at all. WHY: a letter is the cheapest place to describe work instead of doing it, and a session amending it while the senior's list sits untouched is doing exactly that.@@ DECISION: do NOT add a remedy line to this guard's message. WHEN: you are annoyed that the refusal names no fix and are about to helpfully add one. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkharness-guards for the seam, then read the comment above the Reason string in Test-WkLetterEditAllowed.ps1 before touching it. WHY: the owner set that tone deliberately and the source says so verbatim -- naming a fix there would just become the next thing a session performs instead of working, and a polite version gets read as paperwork and answered with paperwork while a verdict on the reader gets answered with work. The gap between the two numbers IS the message.@@ THE PUSH BRANCH HAS A DIFFERENT SKILL CATALOGUE, so an anchor that resolves on your working branch can fail on the very commit that lands the letter. Measured 2026-09-11 in WkAutoQuant: a letter passing the anchor gate locally with 0 unanchored paragraphs was refused at push with 12, and every failing id was one added or re-tiered recently -- wk-pnl-howto, wk-chart, letter-edit-howto, willkim-scalp-buy-side-howto. wkpush_minimal cuts a fresh branch from origin/main, so the catalogue the gate consults there is origin's, not yours. THE FIX IS CHEAP ONCE YOU KNOW IT: anchor to CORE ids that have been on the remote for a while, and when you want a satellite tier say so in the sentence instead of in the pointer -- read wk-selftest step 11 rather than pointing at wk-pnl-howto. THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME LESSON, measured the same hour: the MANIFEST checker's session window on the push branch also starts LATER than your own session, so rows naming files you committed hours earlier are refused as not yours while the newest two pass. Keep the table to the last commits and name the rest in PROSE, which only handoff-names reads. BOTH FAILURES SHARE ONE CAUSE: the gate does not run where you are standing, so verify the letter by PUSHING it, never by the local anchor count. THE MANIFEST GATE READS THE WHOLE FILE, and it reports ONLY THE FIRST unverifiable quote per attempt -- a TOKEN-BURN BUG the owner named on 2026-09-10: seven bad rows in one letter cost seven full commit-plus-grep round trips, because every refusal names one row and one skill and then stops. It should collect every failing row and print them together. UNTIL IT DOES, THE REMEDY IS ON THE WRITER: grep each named skill file for its row's quote yourself in ONE pass before attempting the commit, since the quote is the one field that cannot be faked and the gate is the most expensive place to learn it is wrong., so a PREDECESSOR row becomes YOUR claim and its own prescribed remedy breaks a repo rule -- measured 2026-09-10, the refusal named scripts/us_buy_amend_decision.py, a file this session never opened, as Row 1. WHEN: a letter commit is refused with MANIFEST BLOCKED naming a file you never touched, and a low row number is the tell that it belongs to an inherited section. HOW: check git log since session start for that path FIRST, and if the row is a predecessor's do NOT follow the refusal's advice -- it says to read the file and add a comment recording what you verified, which is dirtying working source to move a ledger, forbidden here by name and settled by this skill's own capital step: source is accumulated capital and the letter is a description of it, so a letter gate firing inside a commit that would touch source is the defect rather than your homework. THE MOVES THAT BREAK NOTHING: retitle the inherited section so it parses as theirs, as the handoff-names entry already prescribes for the sibling gate, or move the inherited manifest table to a dated sidecar -- migrating its skill ids into your names list FIRST, or the names gate then blocks on ids that were never yours. THE SEAM FOR WHOEVER FIXES IT: scope the manifest scan to the section written since the last HANDOFF.md commit, the same boundary the owner approved for the .tmp proto arm, so each interval is owned by exactly one letter writer. THE COUNT MOVES ON A MANIFEST ROW, NOT ON A COMMIT -- so a fix that is committed and pushed still reads unanswered until its row is written. That was a live deadlock until step 3 reordered the rules; it is history now, kept as one line because the ROW-not-commit fact is still true and still surprises. //why:just made the unmeasurable-wish-count and missing-module branches fail-closed instead of silently allowing, per owner directive 2026-09-14-sonnet //why:just made the unmeasurable-wish-count and missing-module branches fail-closed instead of silently allowing, per owner directive 2026-09-14-sonnet

BUG: a wish can name a file the answering repo does not own, and then NEITHER letter can close it -- measured 2026-09-02, unresolved. WHEN: wkwish run in repo A names a source file that lives in repo B, which is the normal case for any personal repo whose harness lives in wkappbot-kih. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto to confirm which file the refusal names, then check git ls-files in the repo you are standing in BEFORE writing the row -- if the file is not tracked there, stop and tell the owner rather than hunting for a wording that slips through. WHY: both doors were tried and both are shut. Writing the row into personal-docs was refused with WIRED file not tracked, git ls-files does not know wkharness-common-dietscore.ps1 -- correct, it lives in wkappbot-kih. Writing the same row into the wkappbot-kih letter was then refused by wish-score-ratchet with was 0 granted, now 0, because that repo's verdict grades its OWN wish list and my row answered a wish belonging to the other repo's list. The underlying fix had already landed and been pushed as f60dbbea5 and was verified by the score difference, 71 for the session repo against 60 for the tool's own repo, so the WORK was done and only the RECORD is impossible. THE SHAPE TO REMEMBER: a wish list is per-repo but the harness sources are central, so any wish naming a central file is unanswerable from a satellite repo -- and the gate reads that as a session refusing to cooperate.

RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by owner directive, and the earlier steps' MEASURED DEADLOCK is now history rather than a live warning -- read this before believing them. WHEN: the gate refuses your letter, or you are about to record another deadlock between a wish count and the file that carries the rows. HOW: run 'wkappbot skill read wkwish-howto' for what the count actually reads, then check the rule ORDER in Test-WkLetterEditAllowed.ps1 rather than the wish percentage -- it is now (1) not HANDOFF.md, none of its business -- and since 2026-09-17 Invoke-WkLetterEditGate.ps1 decides this from the leaf name BEFORE its git rev-parse and wish-count refresh, because running that work first on every Write pushed the hook past its 25 s budget (g-after-letteredit 25193-25980 ms) and refused unrelated .tmp writes; (2) first letter of the session, allowed; (3) tracked uncommitted work outside the letter, ALLOWED because the letter is then a receipt for something that exists; (4) clean tree and wishes under half, still REFUSED. WHY: the loop was real and closed -- wkwish grants a wish only for a manifest row, the row lives in HANDOFF.md, and the gate refused HANDOFF.md until the count rose, with the session-start exemption already spent after the session's first letter commit. wish-score-ratchet.sh settles which side was wrong: it exists to permit an interim letter commit whenever the score improves, and it can NEVER fire if the edit producing that improvement is refused. Two parts of one machine were giving opposite orders. The intent is unchanged -- what is forbidden is writing INSTEAD of working -- and the proof is the refusals, verified in an isolated repo with hooks disabled: skill-only dirt refuses, letter-only dirt refuses, real source dirt allows. Live result: 4/12 granted opened the letter, rows landed, ratchet reported 'wish score improved: 0 -> 5', commit 77470c69d. //why:landed the cache-regeneration fix for the deadlock this step records -- regenerate via the real decider instead of trusting a stale cache-sonnet

OWNER PROCEDURE 2026-09-07, given verbatim when a session was stuck at this gate and is the shortest path through it: to write in the letter you must delete the senior paragraph, and the order is GRANT THE SENIOR WISH, WRITE THE WIRED SOURCE NAME INTO THE MANIFEST, THEN DELETE THE PARAGRAPH -- CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 in WKAppBot: with a clean tree (only skill.json mirrors dirty), rule 3 stayed refused across two retries; removing ONE dead CLAUDE.md study-lock (a real, non-skills/memory tracked file) as the tree's only outstanding change is what let the very next HANDOFF.md edit through, closing 4 more wishes in one pass. His words: to write in the letter you will have to delete the senior paragraph, so grant the senior wish, write the wired source name in the manifest, and then delete the paragraph. WHEN: the gate refuses HANDOFF.md with POOR COOPERATION and N of M wishes granted, and you are about to hunt for a wording that slips through or to report a deadlock. HOW: run 'session_init_path=D:/GitHub/wkappbot-kih/.githooks/lib/session-init.sh bash D:/GitHub/wkappbot-kih/.githooks/lib/handoff-wish-verdict.sh' to see WHICH ONE wish is open -- it names exactly one file and prints a SKELETON ROW with FILL placeholders -- then do the work on that file, add the manifest row naming the file you actually wired, and only then remove the senior paragraph that wish came from. The paragraph is deleted LAST because it is the receipt being consumed, not a chore being skipped. WHY: the earlier steps here record three deadlocks and each was read as the machine being broken, when the missing piece was the ORDER. A session that deletes the paragraph first has destroyed the record of a wish it has not answered, and one that edits the letter first is doing the exact thing the gate exists to stop -- writing instead of working. The wish is closed by DOING, the row is what makes the doing legible, and the deletion is the last step because by then it records nothing that is still owed. AND THE PRECONDITION STEP 2 ALREADY NAMES STILL HOLDS: check 'git ls-files' for the named file in the repo you are standing in BEFORE writing the row -- a wish naming a central harness file is unanswerable from a satellite repo, and that is a report to the owner rather than a wording problem. READ THIS STEP BEFORE YOUR FIRST ATTEMPT, NOT AFTER YOUR THIRD -- the ORDER is the whole answer and every session that met this gate paid several refusals to learn it.

INCIDENT: the restoration this repo's own wish tool DEMANDS is refused by this gate -- a new form of the deadlock steps 1 and 2 already record. WHEN: wkwish prints the senior's deleted paragraphs and tells you to put them back, and your attempt to do exactly that is refused with POOR COOPERATION. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkwish for the tool's contract and wkappbot skill read claude-session-handoff for where the letter sits in the descent, then STOP and report it to the owner rather than routing around it -- the three available exits are all wrong and naming that is the correct move. WHY: rule 3 opens the letter only while TRACKED UNCOMMITTED WORK sits outside it, so a session that commits diligently as it goes closes its own door. NONE OF THE OBVIOUS EXITS IS LEGITIMATE -- checking out an older letter discards a day of current work, dirtying an unrelated source to satisfy rule 3 is gaming the gate, and clearing half the senior list is not a thing to start late in a session. THE PAIR CAN LOOK UNSATISFIABLE AND IS NOT -- proven through 2026-09-13. Once letter-edit refuses on a clean tree, fat-md-growth's remedy reads as unreachable, since compressing IS an edit. The way out is that a letter edit is allowed while YOUR OWN uncommitted source sits in the tree, so land source and letter in alternation rather than clearing the tree first. A third rung compounds it: wish-score-ratchet reads the WORKING COPY rather than the index, so a dirty letter refuses an UNRELATED source commit -- THE CORRECT MOVE IS TO UNSTAGE THE LETTER AND COMMIT THE SOURCE ALONE -- git restore --staged HANDOFF.md, then commit, and the same commit passes unchanged. BETTER STILL, NEVER STAGE IT: owner 2026-09-14, who watched a session run git add HANDOFF.md followed by git commit sixteen times. Pass the PATHSPEC straight to commit -- git commit HANDOFF.md -F .tmp/msg.txt -- which commits that path from the WORKING TREE without touching the index at all. Two wins, and the second is the one that matters: it is one command instead of two, and it leaves the index CLEAN, so the staged-letter trap above cannot form in the first place. A letter left staged by an earlier failed attempt silently attaches the whole letter ladder to your next unrelated SOURCE commit, and git restore --staged does not survive a later git add of the same file -- so the cure is to never create the condition. Check with git diff --cached --name-only before any source commit; if HANDOFF.md appears there, some earlier round staged it. Verified repeatedly 2026-09-13. Do NOT reach for stash here: this repo's own record has a predecessor fix lost that way nine times over, and the letter is the one file you cannot afford to drop. THE ONE-CONDITION FIX, and it neither weakens the gate nor needs new machinery: Test-WkLetterHasUnrecordedWork asks IS THERE WORK IN THE TREE when the question it means is HAS THIS SESSION DONE WORK. Add a second arm for work COMMITTED since session start outside the letter -- that file already resolves sessionStartUtc and already runs git log --since against HANDOFF.md a few lines above, so both parts exist. A session that has genuinely done nothing still has no commits and stays refused, so the purpose survives intact. BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-09-08, WIRING HANDED OVER RATHER THAN LANDED. The predicate exists as a proto with a 14-case suite at personal-docs/.tmp/Test-WkLetterHasCommittedWork-proto.ps1 and -selftest.ps1: 14 of 14, and the INVERSION is real -- disabling the filter drops it to 5 of 14 and, critically, the case named CASE_letter_only_session_still_refused is among the failures, which is the whole safety property. It exposes a PURE decision, Test-WkLetterCommittedPathCounts, plus a set form and a thin git wrapper that FAILS CLOSED, so the decision is testable without a repo. Exclusions mirror the sibling deliberately: HANDOFF.md, HANDOFF sidecars, skills, memory, dot-claude and dot-codex and dot-agents, and dot-tmp protos -- so there is no surface on which a session can look busy without doing work. THE EXACT SEAM, one edit at the existing unrecorded-work call: hoist the repo root into a variable, keep the current call unchanged as the first arm, and add a second arm calling Test-WkLetterHasCommittedWork with that root and the sessionStartUtc the function has ALREADY resolved a few lines above, each arm returning Allowed true; add the module load as a Test-Path-guarded dot-source at FILE scope, never inside the function, so a missing module falls through to today's behaviour. WHY IT WAS NOT LANDED BY THE SESSION THAT BUILT IT: the host lives in another repo, whose working tree carried 34 dirty tracked files on a side branch at the time -- in-flight work that session could not see -- and foundation-is-roots-charge-not-a-chore step 10 rules that a cross-repo change is a REPORT with file, line and evidence rather than a commit into a tree whose state you do not know. The owner had authorised the fix; the boundary is about safety, not permission, and the artifact is complete and portable so landing it is one edit. VERIFY BY WHAT IT STILL REFUSES -- a clean tree with no commits this session must remain blocked, or the fix has removed the gate instead of correcting it. THE SHAPE WORTH KEEPING, CORRECTED 2026-09-13: when a gate blocks the remedy another gate demands, FIRST ask whether the block is truly self-sealing -- most are not. This pair is not, and the letter lands by alternating source and letter commits. A ring that IS self-sealing has a tell: the check that reports the problem also disables the mechanism that would show it fixed. Only then report the pair and name which rule fired. Reporting a ring that has an exit is how a successor learns to give up early.

COMPRESSING AN OLD LETTER IS WISH ERASURE: the archive sections at the bottom are still senior paragraphs, so folding three of them into a pointer was refused as 39 erased wishes and had to be restored from the wkedit .bak copy -- when fat-md-growth demands bytes, cut YOUR OWN prose or move it into a skill, never a predecessor section, and take the backup path seriously because the restore is otherwise unrecoverable. MANIFEST ROWS ARE CHECKED MECHANICALLY: the FUNCTION column must be a bare identifier the named file really defines (the gate greps its def line and refuses a prose summary such as sync_paths depth=1 plus assault 4/4), the FILENAME column must be ONE tracked file rather than several joined by a separator, and every row must name a file some commit of THIS session touched -- measured 2026-09-18, a letter came back with eleven MANIFEST BLOCKED lines, every one a formatting fault rather than a false claim, so grep the def lines first and move assault counts and commit hashes into the paragraph body. MEASURED 2026-09-07, the SECOND gate on the same file and the one that decides how a letter may be written at all: fat-md-growth refuses any commit in which a markdown file already past 32768 measured bytes GETS LARGER. HANDOFF.md sat at 33594 and every attempt to append a descent section was refused, twice, with the added-byte count printed. WHEN: your letter edit passed letter-edit and the COMMIT is then refused naming HANDOFF.md and a byte count. HOW: the letter must SHRINK, so fold the OLDEST section into a pointer rather than trimming the newest. OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-13, AND IT IS A STANDING RULE RATHER THAN A TIP: EVERY INSTRUCTION THE OWNER GIVES DURING A SESSION IS WRITTEN INTO THE LETTER'S WISH LIST, not only into whatever skill holds its detail. He had to ASK whether his own instructions had been recorded, which is the defect -- an item living only in a skill is an item nobody is TOLD to want, because the wish list is what a successor reads first and the skill is what they open once something sends them there. THE TEST, applied before any descent closes: for every instruction the owner gave this session, name the wish-list paragraph carrying it. Detail still belongs in the skill and the wish paragraph still carries its pointer; what may never happen is the wish list staying silent about something he asked for. THE ESCAPE THAT WORKED, MEASURED 2026-09-13 FROM 7843 EXCESS BYTES TO A LANDED LETTER, and the moves are ranked by bytes-per-round so a successor spends rounds where they pay. RANK 1, MOVE THE PASSAGE INTO A SKILL AND LEAVE A POINTER: the single biggest cut, and it is the gate's own printed remedy -- a performance finding worth a full paragraph became three lines plus a skill id, and it is BETTER placed, since a skill is retrieved when relevant while the letter is charged to every session. If the target skill scores under 70 use --find/--replace to merge into an existing step rather than --add-step, which the tier guard refuses and which would sink the skill further. RANK 2, DELETE A PARAGRAPH WHOSE FACT IS ALREADY IN A MANIFEST ROW: about a thousand bytes in one round. The row carries the commit sha permanently, so the prose was saying the same thing twice -- keep only the RULE that commit bought. RANK 3, A WISH YOU EXECUTED THIS SESSION IS THE CHEAPEST CUT OF ALL: delete the instruction, keep only the rules it produced, and the paragraph shrinks while becoming MORE accurate. RANK 4, MERGE MANIFEST ROWS WITHOUT LOSING ONE SHA -- eight rows became four and every hash survived, because the receipt is the hash and not the sentence beside it. RANK 5, REWORDING SENTENCES: a hundred to three hundred bytes a round, which at three minutes a commit is the trap -- do it only for the last few hundred bytes. TWO RULES THAT SAVE WHOLE ROUNDS. FIRST, EXPECT A LADDER AND BUDGET FOR IT: the rungs came in the order wish-ratchet, then anchor, then size, each refusal naming only its own rung, so clearing one reveals the next rather than ending the work. SECOND, RE-CHECK ANCHORS AFTER EVERY TRIM: compressing a paragraph can drop the backticked filename it was anchored on and manufacture a NEW unanchored paragraph, and a FOLDER path never satisfies that gate -- it wants a file that exists. Restore any senior text first, then cut only your own -- a line reading Full text plus git show of that sha on HANDOFF.md preserves every word permanently and costs one line, and the section you are adding is the one the successor actually needs. THE LADDER DECIDES WHAT MAY BE FOLDED, and this repo already states it: HANDOFF prose sits BELOW CLAUDE.md Pending, which is loaded into every session, so any OPEN item already mirrored in Pending is safe to fold because the successor still meets it -- and meets it every session instead of once. Check that mirror BEFORE folding, never after. NEW PROSE GOES INTO A SKILL rather than into the letter: a skill is retrieved when relevant while a letter is read once, so a directive set with commands and traps becomes a skill add plus a three-line pointer, and the pointer keeps only what a reader needs BEFORE opening it. AND SED IS REFUSED HERE -- sed-guard blocks in-place edits, so fold with the Edit tool or with wkappbot file edit. THE TRAP THAT COSTS A ROUND: the refusal counts the diff against HEAD, not against the working copy, so an uncommitted section inherited from a previous session is charged to YOUR commit -- measure the committed size with git show HEAD on HANDOFF.md and the working size with wc, and compare them BEFORE deciding how much to cut, or you will trim your own section and still be refused.

TWO GUARDS GIVE OPPOSITE ORDERS ON THE SAME PARAGRAPH, measured 2026-09-07 and unresolved -- this is the same class letter-edit step 4 already fixed once, recurring on a different pair. WHEN: the Stop frame tells you 'Proved a wish WRONG? Still a closure -- receipt it, DELETE ITS PARAGRAPH', and your deletion of that exact paragraph is refused by wish-gate. HOW: do NOT hunt for a wording that slips through and do NOT delete more -- run the verdict directly with 'session_init_path=<repo>/.githooks/lib/session-init.sh bash <repo>/.githooks/lib/handoff-wish-verdict.sh' and read which ONE paragraph it names, then receipt the disproof in a SIDE FILE the gate does not hold (a dated manifest sidecar) and report the pair to the owner. WHY, with the arithmetic that makes it structural rather than incidental: the wish counter scores a wish WIRED only when a commit TOUCHES the named file, so a wish closed by DISPROOF scores zero by construction -- there is nothing to change in a file that is already correct. Four inherited wishes were disproven by measurement in one session (a suite already fixed, a refusal alive via an EXTRACTED module, a scorer that was only unloaded in the probe, and verb forms that already existed) and the counter moved for NONE of them. It moved only for a file that received a real comment correction. AND IT IS WORSE THAN ZERO -- measured 2026-09-14, the receipt ADDS a debt. Get-WkDescentPassState.ps1 line 345 builds the Stop frame as granted over total NAMED FILES TOUCHED BY A COMMIT THIS SESSION, so a wish is any file path appearing anywhere in the letter's prose. A manifest row is worthless unless it names the suite that proved the disproof, so citing Test-WkBriefGates-selftest.ps1 as the EVIDENCE that a wish was already wired REGISTERED THAT SELFTEST AS A NEW WISH: the frame went from 54 wishes with 3 unwired to 55 with 4, the fourth being the proof itself. RUNNING a suite is not TOUCHING a file, so an honest receipt can never grant its own name and every citation you add makes the ratio worse. WHAT TO DO ANYWAY: cite the suite's OUTPUT LINE and the CALLER's line number rather than leaning on the path -- RESULT: 17 PASS, 0 FAIL with the seam at wkharness-claude-main.ps1:857, or SUMMARY: PASS (24/24) with its two inversion controls -- and let the cited path sit in the unwired list. DO NOT DELETE THE CITATION TO TIDY THE COUNT: the count is wrong and the receipt is right, and a successor who cannot see which suite proved the claim re-derives it from nothing. THE FIX IS IN THE SCANNER, not in how letters are written: a path inside a manifest row or a receipt is a CITATION and must not enter the wish set, the same distinction that file already draws in its own comments where a coincidental suffix match made a wish named Recent.ps1 match the unrelated Invoke-WkHippoRecent.ps1. THE TRAP THAT FOLLOWS, and it is the reason this step exists: the only remaining way to raise the number is to write comments into files you have verified are already correct, which is precisely the 'comment written to move a counter' this repo forbids by name. So the gate's demand and the repo's rules point in opposite directions, and a session that satisfies the gate has broken a rule. Report it; do not resolve it yourself. THE PRECISE SEAM for whoever fixes it: the counter lives behind Invoke-WkWishGateSeam.ps1 and the decider is .githooks/lib/handoff-wish-verdict.sh -- the missing concept is a VERDICT of closure, so that a disproof receipted with evidence counts as an answered wish rather than as silence.

THE ONE-GO RECIPE THAT LANDED 5608c2dc ON THE FIRST TRY, 2026-09-14 personal-docs, success first. (1) Commit every source and skill file by pathspec before touching the letter, so no edit is refused for loose work. (2) If wish-score-ratchet shows the same number as the prior same-session letter commit, stop editing prose and close one senior wish with real source: run wkwish.cmd, do the runnable half of the first unanswered file (tools/court_pdf.py gained --date while the date itself stays the owner's), verify, commit -- wkwish then printed 60 unanswered instead of 61. (3) Stage the letter once and run all four checks on the STAGED copy together: git show :HANDOFF.md byte measure against HEAD, handoff-names-gate.sh --committed, handoff-anchor-gate.sh, handoff-manifest-gate.sh; fix every refusal in ONE edit round. (4) Commit the index once: ratchet ALLOW 10 to 11, landed, pushed. Piece commits earlier the same day had each become the next baseline, which is what made the letter look uncommittable. WHY A LETTER COMMIT CANNOT BE DONE IN ONE GO, answered 2026-09-14 because the owner asked and the answer is three compounding defects rather than one. FIRST, the wish-erased gate names ONE paragraph per round, so the round count equals the erasure count -- that is the bundling defect, and its fix is a single-line replacement in wish-deleted-credit.sh copying a loop that already sits forty lines above it in the same file. SECOND, you cannot learn the list in advance: a git diff against the session baseline gives every paragraph REMOVED, while the gate counts only those whose named files still owe work, so a batch restore of ten moved the count by exactly one. THIRD, each round costs a full hook ladder of about four minutes, dominated by an identity resolution measured at 3189 ms. NONE OF THE THREE IS MYSTERIOUS AND ALL THREE ARE RECORDED -- which is the point: a session that inherits them and does not fix them pays the same tax again, and sixteen rounds is what that tax looks like. AND ONE OF THE THREE WAS SELF-INFLICTED, kept here because it is the cheapest to avoid: swapping a manifest row's SKILL column onto a skill another row already cited took granted from 8 to 4, because the counter rewards DISTINCT named skills and files. Never trade a citation's distinctness for a passing quote. WHEN TWO GATES REFUSE TOGETHER, WORK THE ONE THAT HAS NOT MOVED -- measured 2026-09-14 over sixteen commit rounds, and it is the cheapest rule in this file. The wish-erased count fell 14, 13, 12 and on down while wish-score-ratchet printed the identical line every single round: granted 8, now 8. I worked the falling number because a moving number feels like progress, and every round of it was prose. The ratchet was the only gate measuring WORK, it never moved, and it was telling me so in plain words from the first refusal. A FALLING COUNTER IS NOT EVIDENCE OF PROGRESS TOWARD THE THING BLOCKING YOU; it is evidence of progress toward whatever that particular counter counts. AND THE PREDECESSOR HAD ALREADY PAID FOR THIS: his letter carried the sentence I ground the letter gates while the owner was asking for sectors, and he had to say so out loud -- a paragraph THIS session had deleted, and then reproduced in behaviour while the owner asked for parallel sectors four times. Restoring it was how I met it again. THE ERASURE LOOP: RESTORE FIRST, THEN CUT ONLY YOUR OWN TEXT -- measured 2026-09-07 over eight paragraphs. WHEN: you compressed the letter to fit a size gate and the commit is refused with WISH ERASED naming N senior paragraphs. HOW: the verdict reveals ONE paragraph at a time, so the loop is restore-it-verbatim, re-run 'session_init_path=<repo>/.githooks/lib/session-init.sh bash <repo>/.githooks/lib/handoff-wish-verdict.sh', repeat until N reaches zero -- and expect the count to fall by exactly one per round, which is the cheapest progress signal in this whole ritual. AND RESTORE ONLY WHAT IT NAMES -- measured 2026-09-14 with a negative control, because the obvious shortcut does not work. The verdict's list is NOT the same as the set of paragraphs a git diff shows removed since the session baseline: it counts only the ones whose named files still have work owed, so a batch restore of ten paragraphs pulled from the diff moved the count by exactly ONE, the same as restoring the single named paragraph. I then suspected the counter was decrementing once per COMMIT ATTEMPT rather than per restore, which would have made every restore theatre. THE CONTROL SETTLED IT: re-running the identical commit with the letter UNTOUCHED left the count at 8 and named the SAME paragraph again, so restoring is genuinely what moves it and my suspicion was wrong. Do not skip that control if you form the same theory -- a number that falls once per round looks identical under both explanations, and the cost of guessing is either an hour of pointless restores or an hour of pointless retries. THE PRACTICAL RULE: restore verbatim ONLY the paragraph the verdict names, one per round; pulling extra paragraphs out of the diff costs bytes against the size gate and buys nothing. A PARAPHRASE DOES NOT SATISFY IT: the comparison is textual, proven twice, so paste the verdict's own output back rather than rewriting it. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS TRACTABLE RATHER THAN A TREADMILL. FIRST, COMPRESSION IS ERASURE, so shortening eight paragraphs scores as eight deleted wishes -- there is no such thing as a safe tidy-up of inherited text, and the only prose you may freely cut is the prose YOU added this session, because it is absent from the committed letter and therefore invisible to the check. SECOND, EVERY RESTORE GROWS THE FILE while the size gate is still watching, so alternate: restore one paragraph, then pay for it by deleting your own additions, and keep ONE copy of the unwired-name list rather than the copy each refused edit leaves behind. THE ORDER THAT ACTUALLY CONVERGES: restore all N first while staying under the size trigger by cutting your own text, and only then compress further -- doing it the other way round re-erases what you just restored and the count climbs again. MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-07 END TO END, and the expensive half was not the loop but HOW I paid the size gate. fat-md-growth prints its own remedy in every refusal -- move the passage into a skill and leave a one-line pointer -- and I shaved CHARACTERS instead, through refusals reading 433, then 207, then 39, then 18, then 1 byte, each costing a full round trip. The owner stopped it in one sentence: move whole sentences out to a skill and point at them. Doing that cleared 1400 bytes in a single edit and opened three gates at once. THE RULE: when a refusal names a remedy, the remedy is the cheapest path even when a smaller edit looks closer -- shaving is a loan against the next refusal, extraction is a payment, and the arithmetic never favours shaving. WHAT TO EXTRACT FIRST, in order: a paragraph that is a RULE rather than a status (it belongs in a skill by definition), then an OPEN item you have actually CLOSED this session (it becomes a two-line receipt), then a narrative whose lesson already exists elsewhere. AND ONE MORE GATE SITS BEHIND THOSE TWO: handoff-anchor-gate counts UNANCHORED paragraphs and fires on the INCREASE, so every paragraph you add needs a source file that EXISTS and a skill id that RESOLVES -- a pointer paragraph you just wrote is unanchored by default, and five new ones took the count 61 to 66 and refused the commit that the size gate had finally allowed..

SUBAGENTS ARE REFUSED THE LETTER OUTRIGHT, owner directive 2026-09-12: a subagent that reaches for the letter is to be blocked. TRIGGER: any Edit, Write, wkappbot file edit or file write from a SUBAGENT whose target resolves to HANDOFF.md or a HANDOFF-*.md sidecar. ACTION: refuse early and EXPLICITLY, naming the file and saying the letter is ROOT's own hand, and name the sanctioned alternative in the same breath -- put the finding in the REPORT and let ROOT write the letter, and treat a blocked commit as a finished round rather than a puzzle. MEASURED THE HOUR HE SAID IT: a sector briefed to change one function signature finished its edits, decided on its own to commit, met the handoff-manifest gate, and spent the REST OF ITS ROUND rewriting HANDOFF.md to satisfy that gate -- trimming a DONE section, then rewriting the manifest to name only its own work, then retrying. Write-freeze denied every attempt so the letter was unharmed, and the damage was the whole round plus ROOT having to stop the task and finish the edit by hand. A GENERIC DENIAL TEACHES NOTHING: the sector read each refusal as an obstacle to route around, because nothing in the message said the letter was not its to touch. WHY ROOT-ONLY AND NOT MERELY ROOT-PREFERRED: the letter is the one artifact the next session inherits as FACT, so a delegate editing it writes into the successor's premises with none of the context that earned them -- and a sector under gate pressure edits the letter to clear a GATE rather than to record the truth, which is exactly the corruption the manifest gate exists to prevent. Same class as subagent-config-guard's refusal of CLAUDE.md. AND THE REASON THE LETTER IS THE CHEAP SIDE OF EVERY COLLISION, which is the same reason a delegate must not hold the pen: WHY THE LETTER YIELDS TO SOURCE, in the owner's own reasoning 2026-09-07, and it settles cases no rule anticipated: SOURCE IS ACCUMULATED CAPITAL -- it was built by grinding in an enormous quantity of expensive tokens, and that cost is already paid. The letter is a DESCRIPTION of that capital. A description can be rewritten cheaply; the capital has to be earned again. So whenever the two collide the direction is automatic: a letter that goes ungraded this commit gets graded on the next one, while a blocked source commit keeps a verified repair sitting in the warehouse for as long as the block lasts, and an obstruction that costs six round trips costs six round trips of the expensive thing. WHEN: any time a letter gate, a manifest row, a size gate or a wish verdict stands between you and committing working source. HOW: commit the source ALONE first, then the letter alone afterwards, and if a letter gate fires inside a commit that carries source, treat that as the defect rather than as your homework. WHY IT IS MORE THAN A PRIORITY ORDER: the same scale resolves cases the priority rule never mentions. Measured the same day -- the manifest gate told a session to add a comment recording what it had verified, into a file it had proved was already correct, purely to make a row score. That is dirtying the expensive artifact to balance the cheap ledger, and the capital framing makes the wrongness visible immediately where the rule alone left it arguable. It also explains why a silently TRUNCATED agent brief is a serious event rather than a wasted dispatch: truncation drops the CONSTRAINTS section while the GOAL survives, so the delegate proceeds to do the forbidden thing to the source -- and what those constraints existed to protect was precisely the capital. AND IT NAMES THE ONE THING NEVER TO TRADE: prose you can re-derive, a manifest row you can re-earn, a score you can raise again. Working source you deleted to satisfy a number is gone, and this repo has already paid for that lesson -- three sectors met a size target by deleting live lines from wkharness-guards.ps1, one of them removing the very line that made a seam function while reporting that only blank lines went.

THE .tmp PROTO ARM COUNTS THE PROMOTION RECIPE'S OWN STAGING FILES, so following the documented procedure is what refuses the letter -- owner ruling 2026-09-10, exclude text and markdown from the block. WHEN: the letter is refused with 'unresolved .tmp protos exist' naming files this session never created. HOW: read the named files by EXTENSION before doing anything else -- a .txt is this harness's own staging half of 'write the content to a .txt, then wkappbot file write --source-file', and a .md is never promoted to source at all, so neither is unresolved work. Measured in WkAutoQuant: 337 files matched the proto-name pattern, of which 34 were .txt and 7 .md and 3 .b64, and THREE OF THE FIVE the refusal actually named were .txt. Keep only extensions a promotion could target -- py, ps1, psm1, psd1, cs, sh, cmd, bat -- which is one Where-Object and the cheapest of the three repairs this arm needs. THE OTHER TWO, both owner-approved the same day. SCOPE THE WINDOW to min(session start, last HANDOFF.md commit), the EARLIER of the two: session start alone leaves a GAP, because anything between the previous letter and this session's start is inspected by nobody -- the previous session ended without landing it and this one disowns it as inherited -- while taking the earlier instant means every interval is owned by exactly one letter writer, and the window shrinks back toward session start automatically once letters are being written again. Get-WkLooseSessionStartInstant in the sibling Test-WkLetterLooseWork.ps1 resolves it correctly and returned a real instant when measured; do not write a second copy. AND EXCUSE WORK THAT LANDED: .tmp is gitignored so the proto itself is never committed, and the trace is its promoted counterpart, so reduce each name to a bare stem and drop it if that stem appears among files committed in the window -- and strip EVERY extension when doing so, because GetFileNameWithoutExtension removes only one and a .skill.json name keeps a .skill residue that never matches. FAIL DIRECTIONS ARE OPPOSITE AND BOTH MATTER: an unresolvable boundary must NOT block, or the session is charged for every inherited file again, while an unreadable git must leave the landed set EMPTY so nothing is excused. FINALLY THE REFUSAL MUST NAME THREE ENDINGS, not two -- PROMOTE it, DELETE it, or NAME it in the letter with your reason -- because with only the first two a session inheriting a wide window cannot write the letter until it clears debt it did not create, and cannot clear that debt without writing the letter.

REFLEX, SIX MOVES, IN THIS ORDER -- do them BEFORE the first commit attempt and the letter lands in one round instead of four. (1) COMMIT SOURCE FIRST, on its own, because the letter gate refuses a letter edit while tracked source sits uncommitted outside it; a STAGED file counts, so unstage with git restore --staged rather than leaving it half in. (2) MEASURE THE BUDGET: compare the letter on disk against the same file at HEAD, since growth is charged against HEAD and a section inherited uncommitted is charged to YOUR commit -- write the target number down, because the refusal never states it. (3) PAY FOR NEW PROSE BY DELETING OLD, and the cheapest bytes are DUPLICATED SESSION SECTIONS: two regret blocks, two remaining-work lists, two awaiting-ruling blocks. Merging a pair is pure gain. A disproved item is cheaper still -- receipt it in two lines and delete the narrative. (4) MAKE EVERY PARAGRAPH RESOLVE: a file that EXISTS plus a skill id that RESOLVES, both in the same paragraph, no blank line between. A skill CREATED THIS SESSION is a local fork the catalogue does not have yet, so cite an established id or commit that skill in the same breath. (5) BUILD THE MANIFEST FROM FILES YOU ACTUALLY COMMITTED, one row per descent step, and grep each function in the file its row names -- a self-test whose body runs at module level defines only its helper, so a row naming main is fabrication. (6) NAME EVERY SKILL YOU EDITED in one list line; the names gate reads the catalogue's own diff and will find the one you left out. WHY THE ORDER PAYS: the bundled gates then report together and one pass clears all of them, measured 2026-09-11 as one round trip against four for the gate that fires alone. Full procedure and the dated measurements: wkappbot skill read letter-edit-howto.
